messages:
maya singh: heads up — marketing just confirmed the APAC promo for next week, looks like a concentrated 6-hour spike each day. Forecasted sessions/min jump ~3.2x on current baseline. do we want to relax burst caps for ap-southeast or handle via routing? :thinking:

samir zhao: agree we need headroom but don't want runaway spend. current burst cap is 2x baseline with 20m cooldown. my suggestion: temporarily allow 2.5x for the promo window, add a hard cost guardrail and shorter holdback window after peak.

maya singh: rough numbers — baseline steady GPUs: 120 GUs (GPU units). projected peak demand: ~380 GU for ~6h/day => ~2280 GPU-hours across the week if we open full burst. cost delta looks like +40% if we let burst fully auto-scale.

samir zhao: to be clear on policies: keep steady-state reservation at 1.0x baseline. burst policy = min(2.5x, regional-available-cap). enforce soft-eviction if we exceed burst budget for >30m. implement automatic fallback to eu-west if cap hit and latency SLO still met.

devops-bot: scheduled: marketing-promo-apac starts 2026-03-25T02:00Z, duration 7 days. Current reserved capacity: 120 GU ap-southeast. Available flexible capacity: 450 GU pooled.

raj patel: i worry about network egress and cross-region failover costs. falling back to eu-west increases latency + egress fees. how about we: 1) open ap-southeast to 2.2x only during local working hours, 2) apply queueing for low-priority bursts, 3) route premium tokens to dedicated pool?

lucy ng: +1 to raj. also propose adding a per-customer throttle for the promo window to avoid single noisy tenants consuming burst. we can do a quick policy change in the autoscaler config.

samir zhao: here's a draft autoscaler change — small snippet to apply a soft cap and cost guardrail (pseudoyaml):

```
policy:
  steady_multiplier: 1.0
  burst:
    max_multiplier: 2.2     # temporary for APAC promo
    max_budget_gpu_hours: 2500
    per_tenant_rate_limit: 60 # req/min
    cooldown_seconds: 1800
    hard_eviction_after: 3600
    fallback_regions: [eu-west]
```

maya singh: that looks sensible. can we add an override for premium customers to always hit dedicated pool (no burst) and mark them as 'sla-exempt'?

samir zhao: yes — add tag-based routing. premium -> dedicated pool, non-premium -> burst-eligible queue.

devops-bot: metric alert created: "apac-burst-budget-usage" threshold 80% -> notify #eng-oncall and #fin-ops.

lucy ng: quick risk checklist: 1) ensure KV cache warming doesn't amplify cold-start latency, 2) check GPU preemption mix (preemptible vs reserved) — preemptibles might drop throughput mid-spike, 3) capacity scheduler should avoid cascading scale-up requests.

raj patel: on preemptibles — propose we cap preemptible share during promo to 10% so we maintain stable throughput. cheaper but risky otherwise.

maya singh: action items: @samir to submit config PR with the soft cap + guardrail, @lucy to add per-tenant throttle rules, @raj to update preemptible mix, and @ops-oncall to monitor the alert. I'll coordinate with marketing timelines.

samir zhao: i'll open PR today and include a short load test with synthetic traffic at 3x for 30m to validate cooldowns. planning to tag @devops-bot run-load-test job. :+1:

devops-bot: run-load-test scheduled: suite=apac-promo-smoke, target=3.0x, duration=30m, start=2026-03-22T12:00Z.

maya singh: perfect. small ask — include cost estimate delta in the PR description so finance can sign off quickly.

lucy ng: will add the per-tenant rules and a short note about KV warming.

raj patel: updating preemptible policy now. i'll post the exact config diff once done.

samir zhao: thanks team. once PR lands i'll run the smoke and monitor the new metric alerts. post-mortem after the promo to solidify a template for future short promotions. :eyes:
